name: NGC 2608, host of SN 2001bg (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 2608, a barred spiral galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: n2608-hubble
story: Arm-like structures sweep around the central bar of this barred spiral, a slightly stretched, smaller cousin of our Milky Way. It hosted the Type Ia supernova SN 2001bg, which made it a target for refining the cosmic distance scale.

claims.text: NGC 2608 is a barred spiral galaxy
It appears as a slightly stretched, smaller version of the Milky Way
Its arms are anchored by a prominent central bar
SN 2001bg was a Type Ia supernova
The Hubble program observed Cepheids in hosts of Type Ia supernovae to measure the Hubble constant; N2608 is a target
